full_text:
criteria in order to qualify for reimbursement: The beneficiary was eligible for Medi-Cal at the time the
service(s) was (were) provided; the claimed service(s) was (were) provided on or after June 27,1997;
the service(s) provided was (were) a Medi-Cal covered service-i.e., a Medi-Cal benefit at the time the
service(s) was (were) rendered; the beneficiary was eligible to receive the service(s) at the time the
service(s) was (were) rendered. Reimbursement to beneficiaries with restricted benefits will be
available only for those specific restricted Medi-Cal benefits; the beneficiary has submitted a valid
claim which includes dated proof of payment by the beneficiary or another person on behalf of the
beneficiary, for the service(s) received (cancelled check, provider receipts, etc.), with an itemized list
of services covered by the payment, and to whom the payment was made; the beneficiary has
submitted a completed STD 204 form; for those Medi-Cal services that would have required Medi-Cal
authorization, the beneficiary has documentation from the medical or dental provider that shows
medical necessity for the service(s);the claimed cost(s) was (were) not required to meet co-payments,
share of cost or other cost-sharing requirement(s); the beneficiary was not previously reimbursed for
the claimed service(s) by Medi-Cal/Denti-Cal, other Medi-Cal funded program, the healthcare
provider or by a third party; and the beneficiary did not have other health coverage at the time the
service(s) was (were) rendered that would have been obligated to pay the claimed cost(s). (Revised
Plan for Beneficiary Reimbursement, pp. 8-9.) These criteria are applicable to claims for
reimbursement made to Medi-Cal managed care plans as well as the DHCS. (All Plan Letter 07-002.)
If a reimbursement claim is deemed complete, but is covered by another program, the Department
will refer the claim to the other program who will then have another 120 days to review the claim.

Here, the Department has not completed review of your claim and 120 day review period has not
expired. As such, the proposed dismissal of your claim will be upheld. While your grievance with the
plan was not responded to within 30 days, reimbursement for medications is not a benefit under your
managed care plan. As indicated by the DMHC, pharmacy benefits are handled by Medi-Cal Rx. You
can continue with your reimbursement claim with the Department. Once the claim is complete it will
be referred to Medi-Cal Rx for review of medical necessity. You can contact the Reimbursement Unit
at (916)403-2007 to determine the status of your claim. Should your claim ultimately be denied, you
may request a new State Hearing at that time.

AB 3275, and Health and Safety Code 1371 which was amended following the bill, are not applicable
to this case which mandates timely payments by Medi-Cal managed care plans for claims for
payment by providers. Further, as indicated above, the benefits for which you are seeking
reimbursement are not a benefit through your managed care plan. Pharmacy benefits are a fee for
service benefit through Medi-Cal Rx so any regulations concerning requirements for Medi-Cal
managed care plans are not applicable to your claim. If you qualify for reimbursement in this case, it
would be through the fee for service Medi-Cal, not through your managed care plan.

Unfortunately, there is no provision in the reimbursement regulations or the Conlan plan to order the
acceleration of a reimbursement claim due to potential interruption in care due to financial barriers
which may carry clinically significant risks. You should ask your provider to submit a prior
authorization request directly to Medi-Cal Rx so that further out of pocket payments are not needed. If
denied, you may seek review of that denial.

The dismissal of your case concerning your pending reimbursement claim is upheld.

035 — Dismissal — Final — Rev 03/2022 (English)
